title: Slice 1: the requirement trace
description:
SF-001 to SF-006: documents compile to a trace, an assessment joins it with bindings, pending entries and monitored ids, the view draws, and a project's stories run in one call. SpecForge runs its own stories through itself.

## Operator decision

2026-11-21, verbatim:

> Yes, addressing those diagnostic issues and building tools and making changes and fixes is a priority. Don't over-do testing, just pin the expected behaviour to act as executable specification, it's should be done on interface/trait/gherkin story levels. Project is my current priority project. Build this without overcomplicating the design and the implementation. you would do strategic thinking and delegate the tactical implementation to subagents.The objective is to optimize my flow.
>
> plan on strategic level and build this (delegate tactical work to sonnet, opus and haiku team agents based on which one is better suited for the task,  the harness blocks report files from subagents - subagents should return findings as text), you do the orchestration, set-up the git, workspace, prepare to run this project to completion (set-up instructions for future sessions)), set-up an environemt that you can run and test in an environment isolated from this, optimize the process for performace, we want quick feedback, I want to reuse existing opensource components, frameworks and libraries, and I only write the glue code to make this project happen

This approves building SpecForge with Symphony as first consumer, the Symphony changes that consume it (story runner, seed summary, recipes, views, the one new dependency), open-source dependencies listed in docs/strategy.md, and tests at interface and Gherkin-story level only. Nothing else: a weakened gate, a removed test or a new policy goes back to the operator.

## Oracle

`just check` and `just isolated check` exit 0 in this repository, with the story run reporting every scenario of specs/ ran and passed and none pending. Red today: every body is `todo!()`.
close_reason: Both children closed with their oracles met

title: Operator: must every bound requirement have a monitored invariant?
description:
Assumed default D4: a requirement with stories but no invariant in the consumer's seed sweep (Symphony: REQ-003) shows `no` in the Monitored column and raises no finding. "Only monitored ids must exist" was settled in the code; the converse was not the builder's to settle.

title: Review findings left open: low-severity edges no story pins
description:
From the independent review of commit cf6f6c8 (2026-11-21). Each fails red or is cosmetic; none is a false green. File:line as of that commit.

- src/trace.rs:154: a nested blockquote keeps its inner `>` in the statement.
- src/trace.rs:139: `trim_end_matches('#')` drops a trailing `#` from a title ("support C#" becomes "support C").
- src/trace.rs:263: an id declared in a second document, with its story correctly under the second heading, reports the redeclaration and also a spurious "does not sit under its heading".
- comments.py:58: doc block comments (`/** */`, `/*! */`) are flagged though they are doc comments.
- src/assess.rs:111: a pending row with no trailing pipe, a fourth cell or an escaped pipe is not an entry; on a not-started requirement it vanishes without a finding. A row inside a fenced example is read as an entry.
- src/stories.rs:112: stale feature files in a subdirectory of scratch are not cleared (the run then reports scenarios the trace does not hold, red).
- Only `*.md` directly in the specification directory is read; `.MD`, `.markdown` and subdirectories are skipped by decision (SF-006), recorded here in case a consumer lays its specifications out otherwise.
- Mutation survivors: clearing stale features, the feature file's name, Background folding, the text after "cannot be parsed:".

## Oracle

For each item taken up: a story under the SF requirement it belongs to, red before the fix; `just check` exits 0 and `just mutants` no longer lists the corresponding survivor.
close_reason: Fixed all 6 concrete Slice-1 edge bugs with pinning stories in SF-001, SF-002, SF-003, SF-006, and comments.py.

title: Slice 3 hardening: stories pin the verification layer
description:
The verification layer (SF-007 to SF-018) passes every story, but the stories do not pin it: `just mutants` on c0cd1dc, 2026-11-24, ran 921 mutants in 56 min, caught 511, missed 280, and 130 were unviable. Slice 1 kills 132 of 153; Slice 3 kills 379 of 638. Several survivors are false greens in SpecForge's own checks (ledger integrity, digest verification, property predicates). Until this epic closes, SF-007 to SF-018 are not ready for a consumer.

## Operator decision

2026-11-24, verbatim: "go ahead, this is a project that you are working on fill the beads for work to do"

This approves filing this epic and its children and doing the work they describe under the authority already in docs/strategy.md (pin behaviour at story level). It approves nothing else: excluding a mutant, weakening a gate, changing a public type after its bodies exist, or adding a dependency goes back to the operator.

## Oracle

`just mutants` exits 0 (or every survivor is a classified equivalent accepted by the orchestrator, per child), `just isolated check` exits 0, and the mutation gate child is in place.
